newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease,firm support seen from Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease,firm support seen from Moscow.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds were quoted lower after Friday's fall of U.S. Treasuries but are finding support from local banks, with the seventh tranche remaining the most actively traded paper, dealers said.
Emerging debt prices fell on Friday after March non-farm payroll figures showed strong gains in average hourly wages which could lead to wage-driven inflation.
U.S. Treasuries were slightly firmer in London on Monday after overnight buying from Japanese investors.
"Moscow pushed MinFins slightly up after a small rise in Treasuries tonight," a Sberbank dealer said.
Dealers said MinFins are firmly supported at current levels, mostly by local banks.
"The seventh tranche has been in the greatest demand over the last few days. It looks like a big order being fulfilled," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.
The seventh tranche used to be the least liquid paper until recent weeks.
